results.title: KNUST, Lands Ministry explore plans for satellite campus in Nzema to honour Nkrumah
results.content: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) is exploring plans to establish a satellite campus in Ellembelle in the Western Region in honour of Ghana's first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah. The proposal emerged from discussions between the university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Christian Agyare, and the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, during a visit to the university on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The proposed campus is expected to expand access to higher education in the Nzema area and strengthen KNUST's presence in the Western Region, particularly within the country's oil and gas enclave. The initiative is also intended to recognise Dr Nkrumah's contribution to Ghana's independence, industrialisation and educational development.

results.title: Fifi Kwetey explains why he is comfortable without a government board role
results.content: The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, says he has not been offered a government board appointment, describing the situation as one that gives him greater freedom to speak independently on issues affecting the party and government. Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said he had neither sought nor asked for a board position, although he would have considered an offer if the role was not full-time. "I've not gone looking for it. I've not gone asking for it and stuff like that. If they had offered, would you have accepted? Why not? I wouldn't have minded. Because as long as it's not a full-time position, if it's not a full-time position that will hold me, I mean, it's not a problem," he said.

results.title: NDC will not shield officials involved in wrongdoing – Fifi Kwetey
results.content: The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, says the party will not shield any of its members or government appointees found culpable of wrongdoing, insisting that President John Dramani Mahama shares its commitment to accountability. Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said the party was determined to seek answers whenever concerns about possible wrongdoing emerged, rather than rush to defend those involved. He said the approach represented a departure from what he described as a previous tendency among political organisations to protect their members when allegations arose.

results.title: Fifi Kwetey admits political mercenaries exist within NDC
results.content: The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, has acknowledged that political mercenaries operate within Ghana's political parties, including his own, warning that the practice undermines party discipline and national development. Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said many people join political parties primarily for personal benefits rather than a commitment to the ideals and objectives of the organisations. "A mercenary is somebody who is literally in it just for himself. If he gets his benefit, he can motivate everybody because all he wants is himself.
